_comment: WC2026 QUARTER-FINAL (QF98: winner of Portugal-Spain vs winner of USA-Belgium). KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets France (who beat Morocco 2-0) in the semi-finals (M101). Routes: Spain WON Group H and has conceded ZERO in the ENTIRE tournament -- FIVE straight clean sheets (0-0 Cape Verde, 4-0 Saudi, 1-0 Uruguay, 3-0 Austria R32, 1-0 Portugal R16 with a late winner; rating 94). The best defence in the tournament plus a devastating attack when the game opens. Belgium WON Group G and arrives with a FIRING attack (3-2 aet Senegal from 2-0 down, 4-1 rout of co-host USA; rating 86) BUT: they CONCEDE in almost every game (2 vs Senegal, 1 vs USA, 1 vs Egypt) and are BLUNT vs organized sides (1-1 Egypt, 0-0 Iran) -- and Spain is THE most organized side left. Class gap ~8 (94 vs 86) -> Spain the clear favourite, and the STYLE matchup compounds it: Spain's airtight block frustrates a Belgium that struggles vs organization, while Spain's clinical attack punishes a leaky Belgian defence. BTTS RULE: Spain a clear favourite; Belgium's attack is REAL and in form (not zeroed -- lambda 0.90, they scored 3+ in three of five games) but faces the tournament's best defence -> mild lean BTTS-No (51.5%), Spain clean sheet 40.7%. Draw/ET tail respected (ET 26.7%, pens 13.8%) -- Belgium survived an ET epic vs Senegal and is tournament-tough. Spain to a controlled win most likely (1-0/2-0/2-1); Belgium's equity is scoring first / dragging it deep. Home = Spain (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

BTTS mild-No (51.5%) per the rule: clear favourite + the tournament's best defence, but Belgium's real firing attack NOT zeroed (0.98 attack, lambda 0.90). _validation: Extended 500k Monte Carlo battery, all vs closed form: 1X2 diffs <=0.04 pts; advancement 68.93 vs 68.98 (0.05); ET rate 26.73 vs 26.69; pens rate 13.89 vs 13.76; BTTS 48.37 vs 48.54; clean sheets within 0.11; expected total goals 2.512 vs 2.520. Over 2.5 first seed read 45.82 vs 46.13 (0.31, ~4 sigma) -- investigated: derive_markets matches the score matrix digit-for-digit (46.1306%), and three fresh 500k seeds gave 46.21/46.18/46.07 (all within ~1 sigma, 0.07 pts) -- the outlier was sampling noise, not a model discrepancy. Closed form fully validated.

_postmatch.result: Spain 2-1 Belgium, the winner arriving near the end of the match -- Spain's SECOND straight late decider (after the last-minute 1-0 vs Portugal). Spain advance to the semi-finals (where they meet France), settled in 90'. Belgium's goal ends Spain's run of five straight clean sheets.

_postmatch.verdict: Clean process hit on side and margin, with the BTTS nuance earning its keep. Spain advanced as the 69.0% pick (✅), won 2-1 (a top-4 scoreline at 9.5%), settled in 90'. The judgement call that mattered: I deliberately did NOT zero Belgium's firing attack (lambda 0.90, BTTS near-neutral at 48.5/51.5) despite Spain's five straight clean sheets -- and Belgium DID score, ending Spain's shut-out streak. A hard BTTS-No trim (treating Belgium like a Paraguay/Ghana-class blunt underdog) would have been wrong; the rule's distinction between a genuinely firing attack (Belgium: 4-1 USA, 3-2 Senegal) and a blunt one held. The mild misses inside the hit: Spain's clean sheet (40.7%, the modal single branch) did not fire, and it tipped Over 2.5 (the 46% branch) -- both were near-coin-flips in the forecast, so neither is a process error. And Spain's PATTERN sharpened: a second straight knockout won with a LATE decider -- they control games without putting them away, then strike as the opponent tires late. Ominously for the semi: that is exactly how you beat an elite defence.
_postmatch.lesson: The BTTS rule's calibration by ATTACK QUALITY (not just favourite status) is now well-validated in both directions: blunt underdogs get shut out (Paraguay, Ghana, Morocco -- BTTS-No landed), genuinely firing attacks score even on elite defences (Belgium ended Spain's five-game shut-out run -- keeping BTTS near-neutral was right). SPAIN PROFILE for the semi-final vs France: two straight late deciders -- Spain grinds elite-level opponents and finds the goal in the final stretch; their advancement converts (69% -> through) but their clean sheet is no longer near-automatic against real attacks. France-Spain is the tournament's two best defences AND two most clinical attacks -- expect tight, low-scoring, late-deciding, with a fat ET tail.
